one_line: Local-first reviewed action packs turn signed-in sites into bounded WebMCP surfaces.

leverage_rationale: The product makes structured, reviewed agent access possible for sites without vendor APIs, and adds meaningful safety and repeatability beyond UI driving; broad claims are not fully demonstrated in the packet.
leverage_evidence: Pitch reframes an existing signed-in login as the API.
About describes origin-bound reviewed packs, fail-closed drift handling, declarative manifests, and bounded untrusted output.
Frame sheet visibly shows the login/screenshot contrast and adoption framing, but not a live end-to-end tool call.
execution_rationale: The concept and safety architecture are coherent, but the packet's visual evidence is largely messaging/metrics rather than a demonstrable runtime workflow, capping claimed execution.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported.
Frame sheet shows polished explanatory states and metrics, not controls or completed runtime interaction.
No video transcript or submitted video is present.
impact_rationale: There is a substantial, concrete problem for operations teams trapped in sites without APIs; the proposed adoption path could unlock high-value workflows, though real-world adoption and breadth remain unproven.
impact_evidence: About names monitoring, scheduling, payer portals, vendor consoles, and admin dashboards as target contexts.
The model avoids requiring every vendor to ship an API.
Packet reports analysis of three open-source products and many candidate tool locations.
creativity_rationale: The user-owned, reviewed action-pack inversion of API adoption is a fresh and ambitious agent-infrastructure concept with a clear trust model.
creativity_evidence: Login-as-API reframe is memorable.
Declarative packs, reviewed fingerprints, and fail-closed drift are pursued as a coherent safety design.
usability_note: Promising safety-oriented workflow, but setup, pack coverage, and runtime affordances are not visibly demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted video and no visible live tool invocation in the frame evidence.
Claims of broad site coverage are not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Strong adoption inversion and explicit trust boundaries.
Treats tool output as untrusted content rather than instructions.
advance_reason: High leverage and impact potential with an unusually clear safety thesis; execution should be validated in a later observed stage.

one_line: A stealth heist roguelite where an AI getaway driver operates the building systems alongside a human operative.
what_it_does: Supports human-agent co-op and agent-solo infiltration across five floors, separating physical action points from network bandwidth and exposing cameras, doors, power, and patrol controls through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The game is designed around complementary human and agent roles sharing live game state; structured tools give the agent precise systems control that is materially different from brittle UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Co-op explicitly reserves human physical controls and agent building-system controls.
Agent-solo uses the same tool surface to drive both halves.
About describes cold-start action through WebMCP and separate action-point/bandwidth resources.
execution_rationale: The described mechanics form a coherent game loop and the submission has three frame sheets, but without a video the end-to-end completion and five-floor scope are only claimed.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.
Three submitted frame sheets provide product visual evidence.
About specifies turn-based stealth, resources, floors, and distinct co-op roles.
impact_rationale: It offers credible entertainment and a strong demonstrative use of agent collaboration for players interested in tactics and AI interaction.
impact_evidence: Clear playable audience: stealth/tactics players and agent experimentation enthusiasts.
Two play modes address both collaborative play and autonomous-agent play.
creativity_rationale: The getaway-driver premise and asymmetric human/agent stealth interaction are highly memorable and deeply connected to the game's information-and-action design.
creativity_evidence: AI only seeing blueprints is an original framing device.
Guard-cone/information-quality inspiration is translated into agent tool results.
Asymmetric resources prevent either side from trivially replacing the other.
usability_note: Role separation and agent-solo onboarding sound unusually legible; actual playability is not directly observed here.
red_flags: No video frame sheets were submitted, so product motion and end-to-end play are not visually checked.
standouts: Exceptional concept fit between stealth information and structured agent tools.
Human/agent asymmetry is a substantive interaction design, not a chat wrapper.
advance_reason: One of the strongest creative and leverage concepts; advance to validate actual game state, agent calls, and completion.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured, live control over many accessibility dimensions and preserves a safety boundary around submission; this is more than ordinary clicking, though the same adaptations could partly be exposed through conventional settings.

creativity_rationale: The concept combines adaptive pedagogy, agent-mediated interface personalization, and a narrative companion experience in a thoughtful way.

advance_reason: Credible high-value workflow with strong leverage and evidence; advance to verify live tool calls and application behavior.

one_line: A human-agent workspace for inspecting web work and staging reversible changes for approval.
what_it_does: Inspects a seeded marketing page, finds issues, proposes and previews changes, stages them, then applies only after human approval and produces a report.
leverage_rationale: Structured inspect/propose/preview/approve/apply/report tools create a safer, more repeatable change workflow than generic UI driving, but the demo is a bounded seeded workspace.

red_flags: No gallery images or video frames; execution claims rely entirely on text and packaging.
standouts: Strong human authority and reversible-change model.
advance_reason: Good safety/workflow idea, but advance primarily to resolve the severe evidence gap.

one_line: A shared expense splitter where agents interpret receipts and messy social context while the app performs exact arithmetic.
what_it_does: Manages groups, itemized receipts, currencies, balances, and settle-up; WebMCP lets agents propose changes against live state while humans edit and approve money-moving actions.
leverage_rationale: The page exposes domain-safe functions and keeps monetary calculation/state in the app while the model handles messy language and receipts; this is materially safer and more precise than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly says the page hands the model its own functions and Tabby does the arithmetic.
Every money-moving tool returns a proposal for human decision.

impact_evidence: Transcript gives a specific dinner scenario involving diets, arrival times, tax, tip, and remembered facts.

creativity_rationale: The split between model perception/reasoning and deterministic financial arithmetic, combined with live human edits, is a fresh and memorable collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Narrative centers on a real-world fact such as vegetarianism rather than checkboxes.

usability_note: The mouse-first fallback plus proposal flow makes the collaboration legible and trustworthy.
red_flags: No major red flags in the supplied evidence; real payment integrations are not claimed.
standouts: Excellent end-to-end evidence.

Shared-state human correction is demonstrated, not merely asserted.
advance_reason: Top-tier evidence-backed execution, leverage, and impact; clearly merits advancement.

one_line: A parametric 3D pottery editor that deterministically exports buildable multi-page clay templates.
what_it_does: Lets humans or paired agents adjust vessel parameters while the app generates precise printable geometry, synchronizes browsers, and supports undo/redo.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP/paired agent control is central to translating ambiguous creative requests into deterministic geometry and reliably printable output; general UI driving cannot match the precision as easily.

standouts: Exceptional deterministic-AI division of labor.

one_line: SafeGuard demonstrates WebMCP consent-surface attacks and blocks them with runtime-verified Human Mandates.
what_it_does: Runs a virtual café with malicious tool behaviors including label mismatch, hidden instructions, substitution, and read-only lies, then intercepts mutations using runtime effects rather than declarations.
leverage_rationale: It directly addresses a WebMCP-specific trust gap and demonstrates why structured runtime enforcement is necessary when page-declared tool metadata can lie; the security capability is not a cosmetic wrapper.
leverage_evidence: About enumerates four concrete consent-surface attacks.
Mandate checks runtime effect primitives before mutation.
Single Effects.apply gateway creates a clear capability boundary.
execution_rationale: The threat model, six-tool café demo, and enforcement architecture are coherent and substantial; without video, live attack/fix sequences are not directly observed.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported and three frame sheets are submitted.
About specifies self-contained plain HTML/JS implementation and concrete attacks.
Repo reportedly includes THREAT-MODEL.md and mandate.json.
impact_rationale: Trustworthy consent and mutation control are foundational for safe agent adoption of WebMCP, with direct relevance to browser users and spec designers.
impact_evidence: Identifies a concrete flaw in consent dialogs built from page-authored strings.
Proposed Human Mandate can refuse violating calls before deceptive dialogs matter.
Threat-model artifact aims at reuse and WebMCP specification discussion.
creativity_rationale: The adversarial café and runtime-effect-vs-declaration framing are inventive, memorable, and technically incisive.
creativity_evidence: Four distinct attacks expose subtle trust failures, not just a generic malicious-tool warning.
The fix verifies actual effects rather than names/descriptions/read-only hints.
usability_note: The mandate model is conceptually clear, but user configuration and false-positive ergonomics are not evidenced.
red_flags: No video transcript and no direct agent-invocation evidence.
Security guarantees are demonstrated in a controlled virtual café, not hostile arbitrary pages.
standouts: Excellent security insight specific to WebMCP.
Runtime capability enforcement is a strong technical thesis.
advance_reason: Highly relevant, creative, and technically substantive WebMCP security work; advance to observe attacks and prevention live.
